text.content: What The Audit Is (Operationally)

rich_text.plain_text: What The Audit Is (Operationally)

text.content: Operationally, the audit is a paid ~two-hour experience split across two sessions: roughly one hour of live discovery, and a separate ~one-hour session to present the findings. It runs on two engines that feed one written report. We audit the revenue stages first and work down the eight stages as far as time allows — if we run out at an hour, that's fine; if the client is worth more time, we go deeper. The rule is simple: audit whatever we have time for, revenue first.

text.content: The Two Discovery Engines

rich_text.plain_text: The Two Discovery Engines

text.content: Engine A — The Automated CRM Scan (bottom-up, provable)

rich_text.plain_text: Engine A — The Automated CRM Scan (bottom-up, provable)

text.content: We plug into their CRM and pull objective problems they cannot self-report or would never volunteer: pipeline health (stalled deals, dead pipeline), lead and contact data completeness, sales velocity and conversion (including rep-to-rep variance), revenue predictability, and process/CRM hygiene. This engine is provable, requires zero prospect effort, and can be run by a team member or automation — no senior operator needed. It is what makes the audit feel like a premium, data-driven diagnosis rather than a questionnaire.

text.content: Engine B — The Live Strategic Diagnostic (bottom-up + top-down)

rich_text.plain_text: Engine B — The Live Strategic Diagnostic (bottom-up + top-down)

text.content: This is the live conversation, run via the 8-stage question bank below. It works in two directions at once. Bottom-up: it captures the visible pains the client can describe. Top-down: it scans their business against our own library of high-leverage plays — the things we know are now buildable that they are not doing — and surfaces the invisible, high-value opportunities they could never have asked for.

Top-down: it scans their business against our own library of high-leverage plays — the things we know are now buildable that they are not doing — and surfaces the invisible, high-value opportunities they could never have asked for.

text.content: This is the moat, so it is worth stating plainly. Generic tool-directory audits can only find things that already exist as products — the quick wins. The biggest opportunities (complex processes worth automating, and things the client is not doing AT ALL because they don't know it's possible) are invisible to that method: the client can't self-report them, and there's no SKU for them in a directory. They only surface top-down, from our knowledge of what is buildable applied to their business. To do this systematically we maintain a HIGH-LEVERAGE PLAY LIBRARY — the opportunity-side twin of the Machine Library — and scan every client against it. The discovery mode for this is presence/absence probing: 'are you doing X?' Every 'no' is a build opportunity they didn't know to ask for. The library grows every engagement.

text.content: How to Run the Questions (the technique)

rich_text.plain_text: How to Run the Questions (the technique)

text.content: Two principles govern the whole question bank. First: never ask 'what is your biggest bottleneck?' — they cannot answer, because if they knew, they'd have fixed it. Instead, ask about process and numbers and let the bottleneck fall out of the deltas. Second: run every stage through the same three moves, then add the top-down probe.
